jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Placebo Group
jokes.joke: I volunteered as a test subject in a medical trial. They told me, "Report any unexpected changes." By lunch my wallet was gone. I reported it. The researcher said, "That's not a side effect." I said, "Great—then check the placebo group for my credit cards."

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Dress Rehearsal
jokes.joke: I went to boarding school, where they give you one key to your whole life. Trunk, locker, dorm, all one key. I lost it in week one. Spent four years asking permission to get into my own pants. Now I'm an adult, and I still pat my pocket every ten seconds like a guy checking whether his entire personality is still there. Spoiler: it's just the key, and I'm locked out again.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Clinical Trial Confidence
jokes.joke: I signed up for a paid pharmaceutical sleep study, and I walked in completely full of myself. I told the head researcher, 'Just so you know, I have twenty-five years of competitive insomnia. Good luck knocking me out.' Thirty seconds after they pushed the syringe, I woke up three days later in a hospital gown, missing both eyebrows and holding a blue ribbon with my name on it.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Blurry Confidence
jokes.joke: Last week I lost my only pair of glasses—pretty vital if you ask me. But I was feeling cocky, so I figured I could tough it out. Next thing I know I'm apologizing to a coat rack for five minutes because I thought it was my date. Turns out confidence looks a lot better when the world isn't soft-focus.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Too Confident
jokes.joke: I was feeling way too confident the other day. I patted my pocket and thought, Relax, I always know where my keys are. Ten minutes later I was crawling around a parking lot checking under other people's cars. That's when I realized confidence is just arrogance that hasn't lost anything yet.

scores.comment: Strong boarding-school specificity and a good 'permission to get into my own pants' line, but the ending adds a weaker extra beat after the best laugh.
The insomnia boast sets up a clean reversal, but the eyebrows and blue ribbon feel randomly absurd rather than causally funny.
Clear and stage-ready, but mistaking a coat rack for a person is familiar territory and the final soft-focus line is more tidy than punchy.
Efficient setup and a polished aphoristic closer, but it lands more as a clever observation than a strong laugh.
Clear premise and a decent final line, but the twist is mild and the wallet theft sits awkwardly in a medical-trial setting.
Good escalation to eyebrows and a blue ribbon, but the timeline is muddled ('thirty seconds' yet three days) and the cocky setup is wordy.
The coat-rack image is a familiar blurry-vision gag and the moral closer explains instead of landing.
Relatable keys situation and tidy rhythm, but the aphorism ending is predictable and feels like a template.
Crisp economy and a snappy final line that turns a clinical trial premise into petty theft.
Nice observation about boarding school paranoia, but it trails off into an overexplained tag rather than landing hard.
Mistaking an inanimate object for a person is an ancient sitcom trope, and reciting the seed terms directly flattens the delivery.
Relatable setup, but the conclusion resolves into an inspirational-quote aphorism rather than a comic punchline.
Clean misdirection from side-effect to theft; mild payoff, solid structure.
Strong pants line, but adult coda dilutes the snap and restates the loss.
Irony lands, yet random eyebrows-plus-ribbon details feel tacked on.
Familiar keys-loss setup; final definition is neat but predictable.
Clear setup and payoff, but the placebo-group twist is fairly predictable and earns only a mild smile.
Strong personal premise with escalation and a relatable obsession; the personality comparison gives it a good closing turn.
Good cocky setup and sudden reversal, though the eyebrow-and-ribbon detail feels random rather than sharply connected.
Clean and readable, with a recognizable mistaken-identity gag; competent but not especially fresh.
